key_insight: The paper shows that certain quantum reinforcement learning methods can be matched by a classical kernelized Fitted Q-Iteration surrogate under specific data-encoding and problem assumptions.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical dequantization pathway for quantum Q-learning, helping engineers assess when classical approximations may deliver similar performance at lower implementation complexity.
method: Assume a uniform generative model with random state-action samples, mimicking large replay-buffer regimes.
Construct classical kernels to mirror the inductive bias of parameterized quantum circuits.
Derive finite-sample guarantees for kernelized Fitted Q-Iteration and identify conditions for dequantizing quantum Q-learning.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports finite-sample theoretical guarantees and sufficient conditions for when the classical surrogate meaningfully matches the quantum method in the simplified setting.
watch_item: The guarantees depend on a simplified uniform sampling regime, so results may not transfer directly to online reinforcement learning or settings without sufficient exploration.
paper_title: Towards Surrogate Based Dequantization of Quantum Reinforcement Learning
